# picaro

> picaro is a declarative PE packer for authorized red team research. It takes
> a PE (or DLL / shellcode) and a YAML plan and emits a packed PE with the
> selected evasion techniques baked into a generated Rust stub.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](index.html): what picaro is and its authorized-use scope.
- [Getting started](getting-started.html): requirements, a first plan, and the build/run/measure commands.
- [Plan](plan.html): every block and field, plus the interactive wizard.
- [Examples](examples/index.html): the runnable plans, recipes and end-to-end tests.

## Architecture

- [How it fits together](architecture.html): the packer pipeline and repo layout.
- [Multi-stage plans](multistage.html): schema 6 `runtime:` — several payloads and living-off-the-land steps in one artifact.
- [Custom stubs](custom-stubs.html): replacing the builtin loader template.
- [API resolution](api-resolution.html): the payload import proxy (catalogue, phases, limitations).
- [x86 support](x86.html): `build.output.arch`, what is ported and what is still x64-only.

## Reference

- [Measurements](measurements.html): phase-by-phase static/dynamic results and the EDR report.
- [Process hollowing evidence](techniques/process_hollowing.html): measured behaviour and remaining work.

## Notes

- The canonical sources are the Markdown files in docs/ plus
  src/techniques/*/README.md, README.md and examples/README.md.
- mkdocs.yml holds the navigation; the per-technique pages, the plan
  reference and the examples page are generated from those files via
  pymdownx.snippets.
- The site is built with Material for MkDocs. The links above are
  site-root-relative paths in the generated site.
